en.headline: Guangdong yachts make first southbound voyage to Hong Kong today
en.dek: A ceremony this afternoon will welcome the first batch under the simplified scheme, with five vessels already approved and 300 captains qualified for local waters.
body: The Southbound Yacht Travel Scheme for Guangdong-registered vessels is holding its first voyage ceremony this afternoon, with acting Financial Secretary Michael Wong and Transport and Logistics Secretary Mable Chan among the officials expected to attend.

The Marine Department has already approved five mainland yachts to sail to Hong Kong today once they complete their exit formalities. Five designated anchorage areas provide a total of 115 berths, and a real-time monitoring system is in place to track occupancy.

Industry representatives said the simplified procedures should attract more vessels. A Shenzhen yacht club executive noted that more than 1,000 yachts are based in the city and that the 300 captains who have completed Hong Kong waters training and examination should be able to navigate safely. A former Hong Kong Yacht Club president welcomed the anchorage locations but said longer-term fuel and supply facilities would help.

zh.headline: 粵艇南下今日首航 下午舉行儀式迎接首批遊艇
zh.dek: 署理財政司司長黃偉綸及運輸及物流局局長陳美寶等官員將出席，已有五艘獲批，300名船長取得本港水域資格。
body: 「粵艇南下」計劃今日下午舉行首航儀式，署理財政司司長黃偉綸、運輸及物流局局長陳美寶等官員預計出席，迎接首批由廣東省抵港的遊艇。
海事處已批准五艘內地遊艇今日來港，只要完成內地離境手續即可。當局劃定五個指定錨泊區，共提供115個泊位，並設有實時監察系統掌握停泊情況。
業界指手續簡化有助吸引更多遊艇。深圳灣遊艇會代表表示，深圳目前有超過一千艘遊艇，而300名已完成培訓及考試的船長應能安全航行。香港遊艇會前會長則指錨泊區位置合適，但建議長遠加設入油等補給設施。
